rows.name: HARWICH
rows.character: Two fixed lts. at Dover- court
rows.description: 624 ft. apart. In one, bearing N.W. by W. ½ W., lead betw. the Inner Ridge & Andrews buoys. High lt. shows from S. ¼ E. to E. by N.; low lt. only shows betw. S.E. ¾ E. and E.S.E. ...

rows.name: North and West Jetties
rows.description: Red lt. on North jetty, shows from W. ¼ N. to W.S.W. Green lt. on West jetty...........

rows.name: Landguard Point
rows.character: One fix. red or br. lt.
rows.description: A red light outside, from Beach End buoy to S. by E. ¾ E.; white to W. A strip of red lt. strikes the N. Shelf buoy to N. by W. ...

rows.name: Cork Lightvessel
rows.character: One br. rev. lt. ½ min.
rows.description: In 4 fathoms, near the Cork Ledge. Gong; warning gun.......................

rows.name: SHIPWASH LT.-VES.
rows.description: In 9½ fms., off N.E. end of Sand. Fog horn 5 secs. every 2 min.; warning gun..............

rows.name: ORFORDNESS
rows.character: Two br. or red fix. lts. (High light to South)
rows.description: Towers, 99 & 72 ft., with red and white bands, S.W. by W. and N.E. by E., 1,430 yds. apart. In one, from S., lead through Hollesley Bay, but very close to the N.W. edge of the Whiting Sand; from N., between Sizewell Bank and Aldbro' Napes, &c. High lt. is red from W. ½ S. to W. by S. ¾ S. over shoals in Hollesley Bay; the rest bright. Low lt. is red over Sizewell Bank, from N.E. ¼ N. and N.E. ½ E. Then masked in-shore. The rest bright

rows.name: Kessingland or Pakefield
rows.description: Red lt. only shows to S.E. through the Gat...

rows.name: LOWESTOFT
rows.character: Upper br. rev. lt. ½ min. Lower red or bright lt. (High light to North) Two red harbour lights
rows.description: In one N.N.W. ½ W. 900 yds. apart. Low lt. is red over line of sands from N.N.E. seaward to S.W. by S., & br. over in-shore channels. Bell in fogs. High lt. br. with lower red lt., betw. N.E. & N.E. by N., as a guide to round the Ness. The red lt. on N. pier is masked in-shore of N.E. by E. ½ E. for same purpose. When red lt. from high tower opens from the northward, haul into red lt. from low lightho. until N. pier red lt. opens, when run for it until low red lt. changes to white. Fog Bell 3 str. ev. ½ min.

rows.name: Corton Lightvessel
rows.description: Fairway lt. in 12½ fms., outside Corton Patch. Half ball below usual ball. Gong; warning gun.

rows.name: St. Nicholas Gat Lt.-Ves.
rows.character: One bright fixed light One red flash. lt. 10 secs.
rows.description: In 10 fathoms, at inner end of channel; one red ball; lights at unequal heights. Gong; warning gun

rows.name: Yarmouth, or Gorleston
rows.character: 1. One fixed tide light 2. Two red fixed lights
rows.description: 1. On South pier; red flag by day; lt. is red with flood tide, but green with ebb........... 2. Leading lts. to clear Caistor Shoal, one on Sailor's Home, one on Britannia Pier.........

rows.name: Cockle Lightvessel
rows.description: In [?]½ fathoms, at East side of North entrance of Cockle Gat. Gong. Warning-gun ......

rows.name: WINTERTON NESS
rows.description: A circular red tower. 69 ft. high; lt. masked to S. ½ E. to Scroby Elbow ........................

rows.name: Newarp Lightvessel
rows.description: In 17 fms. at N. end of Sand, with 3 masts and balls. Lt. gives 3 flashes in quick succession once in every minute, and interval of 36 secs. Gong or Fog-trumpet, 3 blasts once in 2 minutes. Warning-gun ...........................

rows.name: HASBOROUGH
rows.description: In one N.W. ½ W. (½ mile apart) leading lts. for Hasborough Gat .................................

rows.name: Hasborough Lightvessel
rows.description: In 15 fms. near N. end of Sand; lts. horizon- tal; two red balls. Gong; warning gun ......
